Football.title: Honeymoon over as Pocognoli's Scotland suffer domestic disharmony
Football.standfirst: Sebastien Pocognoli is left with questions to answer after an inert Scotland performance leaves him still searching for his first home win, writes Tom English.

articles.title: Honeymoon over as Pocognoli's Scotland suffer domestic disharmony
articles.standfirst: Sebastien Pocognoli is left with questions to answer after an inert Scotland performance leaves him still searching for his first home win, writes Tom English.

gist: Scotland lost two to one against Slovenia at Hampden.
New boss Sebastien Pocognoli faced sharp criticism after the dismal display.
The defeat put Scotland's bid for second place in jeopardy.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Scotland suffered a one-two defeat against Slovenia at Hampden on a dismal night. Slovenia carved out numerous chances, exploiting vast spaces in midfield and at the back. Ryan Christie scored for Scotland, but defensive frailties allowed Aljosa Matko and Danijel Sturm to secure a deserved victory for the visitors.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The damaging defeat threatens Scotland's bid for second place in their Nations League group and a favourable pot two seeding for December's Euros draw. It undermined the recent positivity surrounding the team and brought an abrupt end to manager Sebastien Pocognoli's honeymoon period.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Head coach Sebastien Pocognoli must nurse his wounds, evaluate his players, and drill his message into the squad. Scotland face their next fixtures in November, playing away against Switzerland and at home against North Macedonia with no real margin for error.

fivew: Scotland's football team managed by Sebastien Pocognoli and Slovenia.
Scotland lost two to one against Slovenia in a Nations League match.
Defensive frailties, a lack of urgency, and tactical exposure allowed Slovenia to dominate.

sections.heading: Why it matters

sections.heading: What happens next

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Daniil Medvedev faced Novak Djokovic in a semi-final match. While trailing in the second set, Medvedev struck a ball in anger that hit a front-row spectator in the face. Following discussions with officials, the umpire disqualified Medvedev from the match.
